title: Projective twisted cohomology and uniqueness of its eventual polynomial
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $N\ge0$, $P=\operatorname{Proj}(k[z_0,\ldots,z_N])$ [def-pc-proj], and $i:X\hookrightarrow P$ a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Let $\mathcal F$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent] of finite presentation, meaning that locally it has a presentation $\mathcal O_X^{\oplus r}\to\mathcal O_X^{\oplus s}\to\mathcal F\to0$ with $r,s$ finite. Put $E_m=\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}i^*\widetilde{B(m)}$, where $B=k[z_0,\ldots,z_N]$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-pc-module-pullback, def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf]. For every $m\ge0$ all $H^q(X,E_m)$ [pqf-def-cohomology] are finite-dimensional, and there is $b\ge0$ such that for every $m\ge b$ and every $q>0$, $H^q(X,E_m)=0$ and $\chi(X,E_m)=\dim_k H^0(X,E_m)$ [def-pc-euler-characteristic]. If $P_1,P_2\in\mathbf Q[t]$ each agree with $m\mapsto\dim_k H^0(X,E_m)$ for all sufficiently large nonnegative integers, then $P_1=P_2$. If $X=\varnothing$, all these cohomology groups and Euler characteristics are zero for every $m\ge0$, and every polynomial agreeing eventually with this section-dimension function is the zero polynomial. This applies in particular to $\mathcal F=\mathcal O_X$.

proof.text: Identify the two twist conventions explicitly. On $U_j=D_+(z_j)$, the degree-$m$ fractions $(B_{z_j})_m$ are freely generated over $(B_{z_j})_0$ by $z_j^m$: the inverse to $a\mapsto az_j^m$ is $u\mapsto u/z_j^m$. On $U_j\cap U_l$, $z_j^m=(z_j/z_l)^m z_l^m$, exactly the transition rule for $\mathcal O_P(m)$. These local maps therefore give $\widetilde{B(m)}\cong\mathcal O_P(m)$. Pulling back its trivializations and tensoring shows $E_m$ is locally isomorphic to $\mathcal F$. Hence $E_m$ is quasi-coherent and finitely presented: on an affine trivializing neighbourhood use the module presenting $\mathcal F$ and its given finite presentation. This is a local calculation, not an invocation of a tensor-preservation theorem.

source.place: Tag 01MS, lemma-when-invertible, with f=z_j and d=1; explicit degree-m chart calculation

proof.text: A field is Noetherian: its only ideals are $0$ and $k$, generated by $0$ and $1$. The cited finiteness lemma is stated on $\mathbf P(\{0,\ldots,N\};T)=T\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}\operatorname{Proj}(\mathbf Z[T_0,\ldots,T_N])$ [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change], which is not given as $P=\operatorname{Proj}(B)$. Apply [lem-nagata-affine-proj-scalar-extension] with $R=\mathbf Z$, $S=k$, $A=\mathbf Z[T_0,\ldots,T_N]$ and the $k$-algebra isomorphism $\beta:k\otimes_{\mathbf Z}A\to B$, $c\otimes T_j\mapsto cz_j$, of [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-scalar-extension]; $\beta$ is graded because it sends monomials to monomials of the same degree. The cartesian square identifies $P$ with its structure morphism $p_B$ to $\mathbf P(\{0,\ldots,N\};\operatorname{Spec}k)$ with its first projection, so the composite $j:X\xrightarrow{i}P\cong\mathbf P(\{0,\ldots,N\};\operatorname{Spec}k)$ is a closed immersion (a closed immersion followed by an isomorphism is again a homeomorphism onto a closed subset with surjective structure map, by the definition [def-weil-closed-immersion]) over $\operatorname{Spec}k$. Apply [lem-pc-m1-projective-affine-finite-cohomology-independent] with $T=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)=k$, coordinate set $\{0,\ldots,N\}$, the closed embedding $j$, and module $E_m$ from step 1. It gives a finite $k$-module $H^q(X,E_m)$ for each $m,q\ge0$. A finite module over a field is a finite-dimensional vector space, proving the finiteness clause for every twist, including twists below the eventual bound.

source.place: Tag 01YS, lemma-coherent-projective (3), in the closed-immersion form

proof.text: Apply closed-immersion Serre vanishing over the Noetherian ring $k$ to $i$ and the given quasi-coherent finitely presented $\mathcal F$. It supplies a single natural number $b$ such that $H^q(X,\mathcal F\otimes i^*\mathcal O_P(m))=0$ for every $m\ge b$ and every $q>0$. Step 1 identifies this module with $E_m$. Thus the bound is independent of $q$, as required.

source.place: Tag 01YS, lemma-coherent-projective (2),(4), uniform bound over the finitely many possible positive degrees

proof.text: The inverse images of the $N+1$ standard affine opens are affine by the affine description of a closed immersion, so $X$ is quasi-compact; since the only opens of $\operatorname{Spec}k$ are $\varnothing$ and $\operatorname{Spec}k$, the structure morphism $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. The closed immersion $j:X\to\mathbf P(\{0,\ldots,N\};\operatorname{Spec}k)$ over $\operatorname{Spec}k$ of step 2 presents $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ as projective in the convention of [def-pc-projective-morphism], hence proper. Properness includes finite type, so finite type over the Noetherian scheme $\operatorname{Spec}k$ makes $X$ Noetherian. By step 1 each $E_m$ is quasi-coherent of finite type, hence coherent on $X$. The closed-immersion cohomological bound gives $H^q(X,E_m)=0$ for $q>N$ even for small $m$. Together with step 2 this makes the defining Euler sum finite. Since $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is one point, sheaves of modules on it are $k$-modules and the pushforward along the structure morphism is $\Gamma(X,-)$, so its higher direct images in the definition are the $H^q(X,-)$. For $m\ge b$, step 3 kills every summand except $q=0$, whose sign is $1$. Therefore $\chi(X,E_m)=\dim_k H^0(X,E_m)$.

source.place: Tag 08AE, lemma-hilbert-polynomial-H0, reduction to H0; coherent.tex Tags 01YS and 01XZ; morphisms.tex Tag 01T6 and lemma-locally-projective-proper

proof.text: Choose a common eventual threshold $M$ for $P_1$ and $P_2$. Then $R=P_1-P_2\in\mathbf Q[t]$ vanishes at every integer $m\ge M$, viewed in $\mathbf Q$. Here is the root argument explicitly. A nonzero constant has no root. If a nonzero polynomial of degree $d>0$ has a root $a$, division by the monic linear polynomial gives $R=(t-a)S$ with $\deg S=d-1$; at any other root $c$, $(c-a)S(c)=0$ and $c-a\ne0$, so $S(c)=0$. Induction on degree therefore bounds the number of distinct roots by $d$. The infinitely many distinct rational numbers $M,M+1,\ldots$ contradict this bound unless $R=0$. Thus $P_1=P_2$.

source.place: Agent argument supplementing Tag 08AE: elementary polynomial division and induction on degree

proof.text: If $X=\varnothing$, a module sheaf has only its value on the empty open; the empty-cover sheaf axiom forces that value to be the zero module. Thus the category of module sheaves is the zero category, global sections is the zero functor, and its derived functors $H^q(X,-)$ are zero in every degree. The defining Euler sum is consequently zero for every $m\ge0$. Apply step 5 to any eventual section polynomial and the zero polynomial to obtain the claimed zero polynomial. Finally $\mathcal O_X$ is quasi-coherent and has the finite local presentation $\mathcal O_X^{\oplus0}\to\mathcal O_X\xrightarrow{1}\mathcal O_X\to0$. Hence all preceding assertions apply to it.

lean.statement: theorem projective_twist_euler_section_uniqueness {k : Type u} [Field k] {N : ℕ} {X : Scheme.{u}} (i : X ⟶ Proj.projectiveSpaceOverAffine (ULift.{u} (Fin (N + 1))) k) [IsClosedImmersion i] (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] [F.IsFinitePresentation] : (∀ m q : ℕ, FiniteDimensional k (projectiveClosedTwistCohomology i F m q)) ∧ (∃ b : ℕ, ∀ m : ℕ, b ≤ m → (∀ q : ℕ, 0 < q → IsZero (projectiveClosedTwistCohomology i F m q)) ∧ projectiveClosedTwistEuler i F m = (Module.finrank k (projectiveClosedTwistCohomology i F m 0) : ℤ)) ∧ (∀ P₁ P₂ : Polynomial ℚ, (∃ a : ℕ, ∀ m : ℕ, a ≤ m → P₁.eval (m : ℚ) = (Module.finrank k (projectiveClosedTwistCohomology i F m 0) : ℚ)) → (∃ a : ℕ, ∀ m : ℕ, a ≤ m → P₂.eval (m : ℚ) = (Module.finrank k (projectiveClosedTwistCohomology i F m 0) : ℚ)) → P₁ = P₂) ∧ (IsEmpty X → (∀ m q : ℕ, IsZero (projectiveClosedTwistCohomology i F m q)) ∧ (∀ m : ℕ, projectiveClosedTwistEuler i F m = 0) ∧ (∀ P : Polynomial ℚ, (∃ a : ℕ, ∀ m : ℕ, a ≤ m → P.eval (m : ℚ) = (Module.finrank k (projectiveClosedTwistCohomology i F m 0) : ℚ)) → P = 0))
